## Definitions

- [passage] Since `{ a : 1 }` is a prefix of `{ a : 1, b : 1 }`, Performance Advisor suggests only `{ a : 1, b : 1 }`. To learn more about index prefixes, see [Prefixes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-compound/#prefixes) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/index-ranking.md#index-de-duplication · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization, { a : 1 }, { a : 1, b : 1 }
- [passage] Hidden indexes are not used to support queries. If you hide an index and observe substantial negative performance impact, consider keeping and unhiding the index so queries can resume using it. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-indexes.md#remove-indexes · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization
- [passage] Since { a : 1 } is a prefix of { a : 1, b : 1 }, Performance Advisor suggests only { a : 1, b : 1 }. To learn more about index prefixes, see Prefixes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/index-ranking/ · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization
- [passage] - A high Docs Examined : Returned Ratio means the query is scanning many documents to return few results, which can be a sign of an inefficient query or missing indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#find-slow-queries-with-the-query-profiler · keywords: Query Insights, index
- [fact] A COLLSCAN node means mongod scanned the whole collection document by document. The official tutorial's no-index example shows 0 index keys examined and documents examined equal to the collection size. After an index is added, examined keys approach returned documents. A large gap between examined and returned counts signals a missing or unselective index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/ · keywords: Compass explain, index, Compass Explain Plan Visualizer
- [passage] `planCacheKey` is a hash of the [plan cache query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape), further distinguished by any available indexes for the shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plancachekey · keywords: Query Insights, index, planCacheKey
- [passage] - Operations that occurred during the period of lag are not replicated to one or more secondaries. If you're using replication to ensure data persistence, exceptionally long delays may impact the integrity of your data set. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/monitoring.md#replication-and-monitoring · keywords: Performance Advisor
- [passage] The intelligent assistant is an AI-powered tool designed for integrated MongoDB development support in MongoDB Compass. It answers natural language questions, assists with debugging errors, and provides guidance for performance optimization. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/query-with-natural-language/compass-ai-assistant.md · keywords: AI-assisted query optimization, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/query-with-natural-language/data-explorer-ai-assistant.md
- [passage] A query shape hash is a string that uniquely identifies the query shape. An example query shape hash is `"F42757F1AEB68B4C5A6DE6182B29B01947C829C926BCC01226BDA4DDE799766C"`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#set-query-settings-by-passing-in-a-query-shape-hash · keywords: Query Insights
- [passage] `queryShapeHash` is a hexadecimal string with the hash of a [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape). For details, see [Query Shapes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp.md#output-fields · keywords: Query Insights, queryShapeHash · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/
- [passage] - Query Shape Reports are not available through the Atlas Administration API. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights.md#limitations · keywords: Query Insights · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights/
- [passage] A query shape is a set of specifications that group similar queries together. Specifications can include filters, sorts, projections, aggregation pipeline stages, a namespace, and others. Queries that have similar specifications have the same query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: Query Insights · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md
- [passage] The $queryStats aggregation stage is unsupported and is not guaranteed to be stable in a future release. Don't build functionality that relies on a specific output format of this stage, since the output may change in a future release. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: Query Insights · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] $queryStats groups queries with common properties into the same output document. The resulting document is called a query stats entry. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: Query Insights · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [fact] Query Insights is a section in the Atlas cluster sidebar that combines Namespace Insights (collection-level latency) and the upgraded cluster-centric Query Profiler; Query Shapes is the default tab. The launch blog is dated 2024-05-02. — https://mongodb.com/blog/post/elevating-database-performance-introducing-query-insights-mongodb-atlas · keywords: Query Insights, Atlas Query Insights and Query Profiler

## Structure and components

- [passage] If you drop an index that is actively used in production, your application may incur a performance degradation. To ensure queries can still use an index during modification, you can create a temporary, redundant index that contains the same fields as the modified index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-indexes.md#minimize-performance-impact-with-a-temporary-index · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization

- [passage] - If `hasSort` is set to `true`, this indicates that the query contains a [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) method. Unindexed [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) methods can be very resource intensive. Check your search index configuration and confirm whether it supports the [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) method. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#find-slow-queries-with-the-query-profiler · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, Query Insights, index, hasSort, true, sort()

- [passage] The order of the indexed fields impacts the effectiveness of a compound index. Compound indexes contain references to documents according to the order of the fields in the index. To create efficient compound indexes, follow the [ESR (Equality, Sort, Range) guideline.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md#std-label-esr-indexing-guideline) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#field-order · keywords: Performance Advisor, index
- [passage] Text indexes support [`$text`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#mongodb-query-op.-text) [queries](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/text-search.md#std-label-text-query) on fields that contain string content. They also support [aggregation expressions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-qe-aggregation-operators) for encrypted string fields in [Queryable Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption.md#std-label-qe-manual-feature-qe) enabled collections. Text indexes improve performance when you search for specific words or strings within string content. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, $text
- [passage] | Scenario | Performance insight | | --- | --- | | You run a query or aggregation without an index. | Add an index to support the operation. | | You run an aggregation pipeline that uses a [`$lookup`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lookup.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-lookup) stage. | Embed related data to avoid the need for a `$lookup` operation. | | You run a [`$text`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#mongodb-query-op.-text) or [`$regex`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#mongodb-query-op.-regex) query. | If possible, use [MongoDB Search](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-search/) to improve performance for text search queries. | | Your database contains too many collections. | Reduce the number of collections. | | Your documents contain an array field with too many elements. | Avoid unbounded arrays. | | The data size of individual documents is too large. | Break up large documents into separate collections. | | Your collection contains too many indexes. | Review your indexes and remove any that are unnecessary. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/performance-insights.md#behavior · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, $lookup, $text, $regex
- [passage] Index filters are set with the [`planCacheSetFilter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/plancachesetfilter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.planCacheSetFilter) command and determine which indexes the planner evaluates for a [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape). A plan cache query shape consists of a combination of query, sort, and projection specifications. If an index filter exists for a given query shape, the planner only considers those indexes specified in the filter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#index-filters · keywords: Query Insights, index, planCacheSetFilter
- [passage] The [Query Profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#std-label-query-profiler) contains several metrics you can use to pinpoint specific inefficient queries. You can visualize up to the past 24 hours of query operations. The Query Profiler can show the Examined : Returned Ratio (index keys examined to documents returned) of logged queries, which might help you identify the queries that triggered a [`Query Targeting: Scanned / Returned`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions.md#mongodb-alert-Query-Targeting--Scanned---Returned) alert. The chart shows the number of index keys examined to fulfill a query relative to the actual number of returned documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting.md#query-profiler · keywords: Query Insights, index, Query Targeting: Scanned / Returned

- [passage] | Field | Description | Applicable Stages | | --- | --- | --- | | `docsExamined` | Specifies the number of documents scanned during the query execution stage. | `COLLSCAN`, `FETCH` | | `keysExamined` | For query execution stages that scan an index `keysExamined` is the total number of in-bounds and out-of-bounds keys that are examined in the process of the index scan. If the index scan consists of a single contiguous range of keys, only in-bounds keys need to be examined. If the index bounds consists of several key ranges, the index scan execution process may examine out-of-bounds keys in order to skip from the end of one range to the beginning of the next. | `IXSCAN` | | `numReads` | The number of documents scanned or index keys examined during the query execution stage. **New in version 5.1** | `COLLSCAN`, `IXSCAN` | | `seeks` | The number of times that we had to seek the index cursor to a new position in order to complete the index scan. | `IXSCAN` | | `usedDisk` | Whether the stage wrote to disk. **New in version 5.3** | `GROUP` | | `spills` | The number of times the stage spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledBytes` | The total amount of data written to disk in bytes. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledRecords` | The total number of individual records spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledDataStorageSize` | The total disk space, in bytes, used by the spilled data. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `peakTrackedMemBytes` | **New in version 8.3** Maximum number of bytes of tracked memory in use by the current query operation. Starting in MongoDB 9.0, the `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, and `UPDATE` stages also report this field. | `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, `GROUP`, `SORT`, `UPDATE` | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: index, release notes, docsExamined, COLLSCAN, FETCH, keysExamined
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, when you run `explain` in a mimumum of [executionStats](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#std-label-explain-method-executionStats) verbosity mode, aggregation stages that use the classic query execution engine output a `expressionEvaluationPeakMemoryBytes` field. This field contains the peak memory usage, in bytes, from expression evaluation during stage execution. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#aggregation-stages-with-expression-memory-tracking · keywords: index, release notes, explain, expressionEvaluationPeakMemoryBytes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] Query shapes exposing field names but redacted values may contain user PII (Personally Identifiable Information). For users without these permissions, Query Shape Insights identifies query shapes by their query shape hash. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights.md#required-access · keywords: Query Insights · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights/

For the components of a command that differentiate plan cache query shapes, see the plan cache query shape definition. MongoDB 8.0 uses the new query shape and the existing plan cache query shape as shown on this page. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: Query Insights · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md

- [passage] The Query Shape Insights table contains one row for each top query shape in your project, where top query shapes are determined by highest total execution time. You can use the Edit Columns button to choose which of the following metrics to include as table columns: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights/ · keywords: Query Insights
- [passage] Field values. $queryStats normalizes field values in a query to their data types (such as number or string) when the query is recorded. $queryStats never stores field values that contain user data. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: Query Insights · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] $queryStats returns an array of query stats entries. Internally, the data structure is partitioned, and each partition will be read at an individual point in time. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: Query Insights

The `key` contains attributes such as: [Query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes); Client information; Read concern; [Collection type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/querystats.md#std-label-queryStats-collectionType) Each unique combination of attributes creates a separate entry in the `$queryStats` virtual collection. | | `asOf` | The UTC time when `$queryStats` read this entry from the `$queryStats` virtual collection. `asOf` does not necessarily return the same UTC time for each result. ## How it works

- [passage] Recommended indexes are accompanied by sample queries, grouped by [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape), that were run against a collection that would benefit from the suggested index. The Performance Advisor considers workload activity across all nodes in the replica set, including secondaries, when generating index recommendations. The Performance Advisor doesn't negatively affect the performance of your Atlas clusters. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md · keywords: AI-assisted query optimization, Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] Each index suggestion includes an Average Query Targeting score indicating how many documents were read for every document returned for the index's corresponding query shapes. A score of 1 represents very efficient query shapes because every document read matched the query and was returned with the query results. All suggested indexes represent an opportunity to improve query performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#query-targeting · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] After you create a wildcard text index, when you insert or update documents, the index updates to include any new string field values. As a result, wildcard text indexes negatively impact performance for inserts and updates. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/create-wildcard-text-index.md#about-this-task · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, Performance Advisor, index, query optimization
- [passage] - Text indexes impact write performance because MongoDB must add an index entry for each unique stemmed word in each indexed field of new documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#storage-requirements-and-performance-costs · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, Performance Advisor, index, query optimization
- [passage] - Create the indexes that the Performance Advisor suggests when they align with your [Indexing Strategies.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/applications/indexes/) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/analyze-slow-queries.md#best-practices-for-query-performance · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization
- [passage] Building indexes when the target collection is under heavy write load can result in reduced write performance and longer index builds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#index-builds-during-write-heavy-workloads · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization
- [passage] When using the default [`maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds) of `3`, the total memory usage for all concurrent index builds can reach up to three times the value of `maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#insufficient-available-system-memory-ram · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization, maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds, maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes
- [fact] Guards on suggestions: no index with more than 16 fields; an index is suggested only if scanned documents minus returned documents exceeds 500 for impacted queries; overlapping candidates are de-duplicated so that prefix { a:1 } is dropped in favour of { a:1, b:1 }. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/index-ranking/ · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization, Atlas Performance Advisor (index and schema suggestions)
- [passage] Although indexes improve query performance, adding an index has negative performance impact for write operations. For collections with a high write-to-read ratio, indexes are expensive because each insert and update must also update any indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/create-index.md#about-this-task · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md
- [passage] You can also adjust the time range the Performance Advisor takes into account when suggesting indexes by using the Time Range dropdown at the top of the Performance Advisor. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#filter-index-suggestions · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] You can create [indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/) suggested by the Performance Advisor directly within the Performance Advisor itself. When you create indexes, keep the ratio of reads to writes on the target collection in mind. Indexes come with a performance cost, but are more than worth the cost for frequent queries on large data sets. To learn more about indexing strategies, see [Indexing Strategies.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/applications/indexes/) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#create-suggested-indexes · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization

- [passage] Building an index in a rolling fashion reduces the resiliency of your cluster and increases index build times. We only recommend using rolling index builds when regular index builds do not meet your needs. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#procedure · keywords: Performance Advisor, index
- [passage] If you decide to continue with a rolling index, consider that they must meet certain conditions to succeed. - [passage] Atlas automatically cancels rolling index builds that don't succeed on all nodes. When a rolling index build completes on some nodes, but fails on others, Atlas cancels the build and removes the index from any nodes that it was successfully built on. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#procedure · keywords: Performance Advisor, index

- [passage] - Text indexes store individual words, not multi-word strings or word proximity information. - [statement] COMPASS-6496 reported that 'Actual query execution time' for aggregations was inflated because it summed per-stage times that already included earlier stages. - [passage] Enabling Queryable Encryption on a collection redacts fields from some diagnostic commands and omits some operations from the query log. - [passage] When you use Queryable Encryption, you define encrypted fields at the collection level using an encryption schema. Encrypting a field and enabling queries increases storage requirements and impacts query performance. You can configure an encrypted field for either equality or range queries, but not both. Configure fields for the expected query type. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md · keywords: Performance Advisor, query optimization

- [passage] A document that shows how often threads use certain internal server locks and how often these locks cause threads to wait. Contention on these locks has a noticeable impact on performance. Use these metrics to identify when coordination points become bottlenecks, such as when contention and wait time increase alongside slower operations or replication lag. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#lockcontentionmetrics · keywords: Performance Advisor, query optimization

- [passage] - [`executionStats.totalKeysExamined`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.totalKeysExamined) displays `3809` to indicate that MongoDB scanned 3,809 index entries. The number of keys examined match the number of documents returned, meaning that the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) only had to examine index keys to return the results. The [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) did not have to scan all of the documents, and only the 3,809 matching documents had to be pulled into memory. This results in a very efficient query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: index, query optimization, executionStats.totalKeysExamined, 3809, mongod
- [passage] When run with an index, the query scans only as many index entries and documents as it returns, resulting in a more efficient query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: index, query optimization

- [passage] The Query Profiler samples operations by using a bucketing algorithm that adjusts the sample size based on the width of the selected time range. To learn more, see [View and Download MongoDB Logs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/mongodb-logs.md#std-label-mongodb-logs) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#data-display-limitations · keywords: Query Insights, mongod · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] To establish recommended indexes, the Performance Advisor uses these metrics in a formula to calculate the Impact, or performance improvement that creating an index matching that query shape would cause. When the Performance Advisor suggests indexes, it ranks the indexes by their Impact. The Impact is determined by the total wasted bytes read. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/index-ranking.md#how-performance-advisor-suggests-and-ranks-indexes · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/index-ranking/
- [passage] To learn more about the command syntax and parameters, see the Atlas CLI documentation for [atlas performanceAdvisor namespaces list.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-performanceAdvisor-namespaces-list/) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#view-collections-with-slow-queries · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, query optimization
- [passage] To learn more about the command syntax and parameters, see the Atlas CLI documentation for [atlas performanceAdvisor slowQueryLogs list.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-performanceAdvisor-slowQueryLogs-list/) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#view-slow-query-logs · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, query optimization
- [passage] To enable or disable Performance Advisor and the Query Profiler for a project, you must have the [`Project Owner`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md#mongodb-authrole-Project-Owner) role for the project or the [`Organization Owner`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md#mongodb-authrole-Organization-Owner) role on its parent organization. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#required-access · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, query optimization, Project Owner, Organization Owner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/enable-disable.md
- [passage] To enable or disable Performance Advisor and the Query Profiler for a project, you must have the Project Owner role for the project or the Organization Owner role on its parent organization. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/ · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, query optimization
- [passage] To learn more about the command syntax and parameters, see the Atlas CLI documentation for [atlas performanceAdvisor suggestedIndexes list.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-performanceAdvisor-suggestedIndexes-list/) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#view-suggested-indexes · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization
- [passage] To view the indexes on the `siteAnalytics` collection, run this command: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-indexes.md#example · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization, siteAnalytics

## Measurements and reference values

- [fact] The advisor monitors operations slower than 100 ms (docs for index ranking) and groups them into query shapes. In the UI the threshold is Atlas-managed (dynamic) by default and can be switched to a fixed value; MongoDB advises not setting a fixed threshold below 100 ms. Changing it needs Project Owner. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/index-ranking/ · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization, Atlas Performance Advisor (index and schema suggestions)
- [fact] 9.0 enables $queryStats collection by default for reads and writes by sampling: internalQueryStatsSampleRate and internalQueryStatsWriteCmdSampleRate both default to 0.01 (1%), so output is a subset of operations. Update, insert and delete commands now get query shapes (8.1 added count and distinct). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/9.0/ · keywords: Query Insights, release notes, Post-8.0 Query Engine Changes (8.1 and 8.2 rapid releases and 9.0)
- [passage] - On clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later, Atlas randomly samples 1% of read and write operations by default. Displayed metric values reflect only sampled operations, approximately 1% of total operations. Query shapes that run infrequently may not appear in the results. This method also collects write operations (`insert`, `update`, and `delete`), which appear in Query Shape Insights alongside read operations. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights.md#how-atlas-collects-query-shape-statistics · keywords: Query Insights, release notes, insert, update, delete · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights/
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, $queryStats collects stats for a sample of 1% of read and write operations by default. To change the sampling rate, set the internalQueryStatsSampleRate parameter for read operations or the internalQueryStatsWriteCmdSampleRate parameter for write operations. Both parameters accept a value between 0.0 and 1.0. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: Query Insights, release notes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] This alert might appear when Atlas automatically [upgrades your search indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/performance/index-performance.md#std-label-index-create-and-update) to enable new features. Your cluster must have sufficient disk space for both the previous and new version of the index. If the rebuild increases disk space use to 90% or more, Atlas increases the cluster storage if you enabled auto-scaling. After the index upgrade completes, Atlas deletes the old version of the index, which frees up disk space. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md#alert-conditions · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization
- [statement] Query Shape Insights (Query Shapes tab) requires a dedicated cluster (M10+) on MongoDB 8.0+. On 9.0+ Atlas randomly samples 1% of reads and writes by default, so shown metrics reflect about 1% of operations, infrequent shapes may be missing, and totals shift after an 8.x to 9.0 upgrade because of the sampling change. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights/ · keywords: Query Insights, Atlas Query Insights and Query Profiler

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [passage] You can use the MongoDB MCP server to get [Performance Advisor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#std-label-performance-advisor) recommendations from your preferred AI tools by using natural language. These recommendations include retrieving slow queries, performing index management, and suggesting schema improvements. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/access-with-mcp.md · keywords: AI-assisted query optimization, Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization
- [fact] The MongoDB MCP Server exposes an `atlas-get-performance-advisor` tool (suggested indexes, drop-index suggestions, slow query logs, schema advice) plus database tools `explain`, `collection-indexes`, `create-index` and `drop-index`, letting AI clients such as Claude, Cursor and GitHub Copilot drive index analysis in natural language. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mcp-server/tools.md · keywords: AI-assisted query optimization, Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization, AI and LLM-Assisted MongoDB Query and Index Optimization
- [passage] To learn more about the MongoDB Atlas Performance Advisor, see [Monitor and Improve Slow Queries.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#create-and-manage-indexes-in-mongodb-atlas · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization
- [statement] Via MCP, slow-query analysis is capped at a sample of the 50 most recent slow queries matching the prompt; this cap does not apply to the Performance Advisor UI in Atlas. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/access-with-mcp.md · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization, AI and LLM-Assisted MongoDB Query and Index Optimization
- [fact] The Performance Advisor's recommendations come from MongoDB's own slow-query analysis; the LLM layer (MCP or Compass assistant) is an interface to those endpoints (suggestedIndexes, dropIndexSuggestions, schemaAdvice), not a separate LLM-based recommender. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/access-with-mcp.md · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization, AI and LLM-Assisted MongoDB Query and Index Optimization
- [fact] Performance Advisor is only available on M10+ clusters and Flex clusters; the Atlas-managed slow-query threshold is disabled on Free (M0) clusters and unsupported on clusters with MongoDB Search enabled. — https://mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization, Atlas Performance Advisor (index and schema suggestions)
- [fact] Schema suggestions flag anti-patterns: unbounded arrays, too many collections, unnecessary indexes, excessively large (bloated) documents, and excessive $lookup use. They come from sampling documents in the most active collections and collections with slow queries, exposed via the Admin API listSchemaAdvice endpoint (Public Preview, Project Read Only role). — https://mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization, Atlas Performance Advisor (index and schema suggestions)
- [statement] Access control: Project Read Only sees slow queries and suggested indexes; seeing field values in sample queries needs a data-access role (Observability Viewer, Data Access Read Only/Read-Write/Admin), otherwise values are redacted. Creating an index from the advisor needs Data Explorer enabled for the project. — https://mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization, Atlas Performance Advisor (index and schema suggestions)
- [passage] For deployments hosted in MongoDB Atlas, you can create and manage indexes with the MongoDB Atlas UI or the Atlas CLI. MongoDB Atlas also includes a Performance Advisor that recommends indexes to improve slow queries, ranks suggested indexes by impact, and recommends which indexes to drop. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#create-and-manage-indexes-in-mongodb-atlas · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization
- [passage] The Performance Advisor monitors queries that MongoDB considers slow and suggests new indexes to improve query performance. The threshold for slow queries varies based on the average time of operations on your cluster to provide recommendations pertinent to your workload. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-performanceAdvisor-slowQueryLogs-list.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-performanceAdvisor-listSlowQueryLogs.md
- [passage] Returns suggested indexes and slow query data for a database deployment. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-performanceAdvisor.md · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization
- [passage] | Method | Availability | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | Use the Atlas Performance Advisor | M10+ Atlas clusters | The Atlas Performance Advisor monitors slow queries and suggests new indexes to improve performance. For more information, see [Monitor and Improve Slow Queries with the Performance Advisor.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#std-label-performance-advisor) | | Check ongoing operations in Atlas | M10+ Atlas clusters | You can use the [Atlas Real-Time Performance Panel](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md#std-label-real-time-metrics-status-tab) (RTPP) to see current network traffic, database operations, and hardware statistics. | | Check ongoing operations locally | Atlas clusters and self-hosted deployments | The [`$currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-currentOp) aggregation stage returns information on active operations and cursors. Use `$currentOp` to identify long-running or stuck operations that may be negatively impacting performance. You can also use the [`top`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/top.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.top) command to get additional operation count and latency statistics.. | | Check server metrics | Atlas clusters and self-hosted deployments | For Atlas clusters, you can [view cluster metrics](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/monitor-cluster-metrics.md#std-label-monitor-cluster-metrics) to identify performance issues. For self-hosted deployments, the [`serverStatus`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverstatus.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.serverStatus) command provides metrics that can indicate poor performance and anomalies for query execution. | | View common query shapes | Atlas clusters and self-hosted deployments | The [`$queryStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/querystats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-queryStats) aggregation stage returns information about common [query shapes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes). `$queryStats` provides a holistic view of the kinds of queries being run on your deployment. | | View index statistics | Atlas clusters and self-hosted deployments | The [`$indexStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexstats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-indexStats) aggregation stage returns information about your collection's indexes and how often individual indexes are used. Use `$indexStats` to identify unused indexes that can be removed to improve write performance. | | View collection statistics | Atlas clusters and self-hosted deployments | The [`$collStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collstats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-collStats) aggregation stage returns statistical information on specific collections and their usage. `$collStats` provides information such as: Storage usage for the collection and its indexes; The average size of documents | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/evaluate-operation-performance.md#performance-overview · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization, $currentOp, top
- [passage] The Performance Advisor automatically analyzes logs for slow-running queries and recommends indexes to create and drop. It analyzes slow queries and provides index suggestions for individual collections, ranked by a calculated impact score, and tailored to your workload. This gives you an easy, instantaneous way to make high-impact performance improvements. We recommend that you monitor regularly, focus on slow queries, and enable the profiler selectively to minimize overhead. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts.md#performance-advisor · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization
- [passage] You can return log lines for slow queries that the Performance Advisor identifies from the Atlas Administration API with [Return Slow Queries](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-listslowqueries). To return suggested indexes and more with the Atlas Administration API, see [Performance Advisor.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/group/endpoint-performance-advisor) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts.md#performance-advisor · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization
- [passage] The [Performance Advisor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#std-label-pa-slow-queries) provides the easiest and quickest way to create an index. The Performance Advisor monitors queries that MongoDB considers slow and recommends indexes to improve performance. Atlas dynamically adjusts your slow query threshold based on the execution time of operations across your cluster. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting.md#fix-the-immediate-problem · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/
- [passage] It is possible to receive a Query Targeting alert for an inefficient query without receiving index suggestions from the Performance Advisor if the query exceeds the slow query threshold and the ratio of scanned to returned documents is greater than the threshold specified in the alert. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting.md#fix-the-immediate-problem · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, index, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/

A query setting isn't guaranteed to be backfilled the first time a matching query runs. - [passage] The threshold determines which operations the Performance Advisor and Query Profiler considers slow. When enabled, MongoDB Cloud uses the average execution time for operations on your cluster to determine slow-running queries. As a result, the threshold is more pertinent to your cluster workload. The slow operation threshold is enabled by default for dedicated clusters (M10+). When disabled, MongoDB Cloud considers any operation that takes longer than 100 milliseconds to be slow. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-performanceAdvisor-enableManagedSlowMs.md · keywords: Performance Advisor, Query Insights, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-performanceAdvisor-disableManagedSlowMs.md

- [passage] - The Performance Advisor cannot suggest indexes for MongoDB databases configured to use the [ctime timestamp format](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod/#cmdoption-mongod-timestampformat). As a workaround, set the timestamp format for such databases to either [iso8601-utc](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod/#cmdoption-mongod-timestampformat) or [iso8601-local.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod/#cmdoption-mongod-timestampformat) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/analyze-slow-queries.md#best-practices-for-query-performance · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) supports building one or more indexes on a collection. `createIndexes` uses a combination of memory and temporary files on disk to build indexes. In self-hosted MongoDB deployments, the default value of the [`maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes) parameter is 200 megabytes per `createIndexes` command. `createIndexes` shares the memory limit equally among all the indexes it builds. For example, if you build 10 indexes with one `createIndexes` command, MongoDB allocates each index 20 megabytes for the index build process. When you reach the memory limit, MongoDB creates temporary files in the `_tmp` subdirectory within [`--dbpath`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-option-mongod.--dbpath) to complete the build. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#insufficient-available-system-memory-ram · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization, createIndexes, maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes, _tmp
- [passage] In self-hosted MongoDB deployments, you can change the memory limit for index builds by setting the `maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes` parameter. Increasing this parameter is only necessary in rare cases. Such cases include running many simultaneous index builds with a single `createIndexes` command or indexing a data set larger than 500GB. You can also set `maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds` to adjust how many index builds can run concurrently. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#insufficient-available-system-memory-ram · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization, maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes, createIndexes, maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds
- [passage] On MongoDB Atlas, the default values of `maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes` and `maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds` vary by cluster tier. You cannot modify `maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes` on MongoDB Atlas. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#insufficient-available-system-memory-ram · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization, maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes, maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds
- [fact] The MCP Performance Advisor tool requires Atlas Project Read Only role or higher and an M10+ cluster, and MongoDB recommends running it with the --readonly flag; read-only mode and disabling tool categories restrict the server so an agent cannot call create-index or drop-index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mcp-server/tools.md · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization, AI and LLM-Assisted MongoDB Query and Index Optimization
- [fact] Docs warn that every extra index slows writes and that the user should weigh read frequency against write cost; the docs also tell users to understand the specific schema warning before changing the schema. Applying every suggestion blindly is an antipattern. — https://mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization, Atlas Performance Advisor (index and schema suggestions)
- [passage] - You can't create indexes through the Performance Advisor if [Data Explorer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui.md#std-label-atlas-ui) is disabled for your project. - [passage] Limits the amount of memory that simultaneous [index builds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-build-process) on one collection may consume for their duration. The specified amount of memory is shared between all indexes built using a single [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) command or its shell helper [`db.collection.createIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes). Increasing the limit may avoid negative performance impacts in some cases, such as when building numerous indexes simultaneously with a single [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) command and/or when working with index key data set sizes that exceed 500GB. The memory consumed by an index build is separate from the WiredTiger cache memory (see [`cacheSizeGB`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-storage.wiredTiger.engineConfig.cacheSizeGB)). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization, createIndexes, db.collection.createIndexes(), cacheSizeGB
- [passage] The Performance Advisor monitors queries that MongoDB considers slow and suggests new indexes to improve query performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-performanceAdvisor-suggestedIndexes-list.md · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-performanceAdvisor-listClusterSuggestedIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-performanceAdvisor-listSuggestedIndexes.md
- [passage] Rolling indexes build indexes on the applicable nodes sequentially and may reduce the performance impact of an index build if your deployment's average CPU utilization exceeds (N-1)/N-10% where N is the number of CPU threads available to mongod of if the WiredTiger cache fill ratio regularly exceeds 90%. If your deployment does not meet this criteria, use the default index build. You can't create a rolling index on an M0 free cluster or M2/M5 shared cluster. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-rollingIndex.md · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization
- [passage] While there is no hard limit on the number of collections in a single MongoDB Atlas cluster, the performance of a cluster might degrade if it serves a large number of collections and indexes. Larger collections have a greater impact on performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md#mongodb-atlas-collection-and-index-limits · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization
- [passage] | Option | Description | More Information | | --- | --- | --- | | Create unique index | Ensure that the indexed fields do not store duplicate values. You cannot perform a rolling build for a unique index. If you enable building indexes in a rolling fashion with the `unique` index option, Atlas rejects your configuration with an error message. | [Unique Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/) | | Index name | Specify a name for the index. | [Specify an Index Name](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/create-index/specify-index-name.md#std-label-specify-index-name) | | Create a TTL (Time to Live) index | Delete documents automatically after a specified number of seconds since the indexed field value. | [TTL Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl/) | | Partial filter expression | Index only the documents which match the specified filter expression. For example: The following partial filter expression only indexes documents where the `timezone` field exists: `{ "timezone": { "$exists": true } }` | [Partial Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial/) | | Wildcard projection | Support unknown or arbitrary fields which match the specified projection in the index. To use a wildcard projection, set your index field name to `$**`. This directs Atlas to use all fields in the document (excluding `_id`). For example: Consider the following wildcard projection document: `{ "product_attributes.elements" : 1, "product_attributes.resistance" : 1 }` If your index field name is `$**`, your index only includes the values of the fields in that projection. | [Create a Wildcard Index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/indexes.md#std-label-atlas-ui-wildcard-index) | | Use custom collation | Create a custom collation for the index by typing or pasting the collation document in the text box. | [Collation Document](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation/#collation-document) | | Create sparse index | Index skips over any document that is missing the indexed field. | [Sparse Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) | | Build in rolling process | Can minimize the performance impact of index builds. IMPORTANT: Building an index in a rolling fashion reduces the resiliency of your cluster and increases index build times. We only recommend using rolling index builds when regular index builds do not meet your needs. WARNING: Avoid performing rolling index and replicated index build processes concurrently as it might lead to unexpected issues, such as broken builds and crash loops. You can only build rolling indexes on M10+ Clusters. During a rolling index build, Atlas takes each node out of the replica set, starts it in standalone mode to build the index, and then returns it to the replica set. This process repeats for each node in the cluster in a rolling sequence. Nodes may appear as down, while Atlas builds indexes offline. This is expected behavior, not an issue. | [Rolling Index Builds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/rolling-index-builds.md#std-label-rolling-index-build) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/indexes.md#create-an-index · keywords: Performance Advisor, index, query optimization, unique, timezone, { "timezone": { "$exists": true } }

- [passage] | **MongoDB Version** | **Changes** | | --- | --- | | 6.1 | Slow operation log messages include [cache refresh time fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-cache-refresh-times) | | 6.2 | Slow operation log messages include a `queryFramework` field that indicates which query engine executed the query: `queryFramework: "classic"` indicates that the classic engine executed the query.; `queryFramework: "sbe"` indicates that the slot-based query execution engine executed the query. | | 6.3 | Slow operation log messages and [database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) entries include a `cpuNanos` field that specifies the total CPU time spent by a query operation in nanoseconds. The `cpuNanos` field is only available on Linux systems. | | 7.0 (and 6.0.13, 5.0.24) | The `totalOplogSlotDurationMicros` in the slow query log message shows the time between a write operation getting a commit timestamp to commit the storage engine writes and actually committing. `mongod` supports parallel writes. However, it commits write operations with commit timestamps in any order. For example, consider the following writes with commit timestamps: writeA with Timestamp1; writeB with Timestamp2; writeC with Timestamp3 Suppose writeB commits first at Timestamp2. Replication is paused until writeA commits because writeA's oplog entry with Timestamp1 is required for replication to copy the oplog to secondary replica set members. | | 8.0 | The slow query output includes a `queues` document that contains information about the operation's [queues](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverstatus.md#std-label-server-status-queues). Each queue in the `queues` field contains a `totalTimeQueuedMicros` field that contains the total cumulative time in microseconds that the operation spent in the corresponding queue. The `queryShapeHash` field for a [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes) is also included in the slow query log when available. If a command with a specific query shape is [rejected](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/operation-rejection-filters.md#std-label-operation-rejection-filters), MongoDB logs a message that states the query command was rejected. The message contains the query namespace, `queryShapeHash`, and the command with the rejected query. MongoDB only logs the message if the log verbosity level is set to at least `2`. | | 8.1 | Slow query log messages contain new metrics if the query execution writes temporary files to disk. These metrics are prefixed by the query execution stage that caused the query to exceed the memory limit. For example, `sortSpills` indicates the number of times that the sort stage of query execution wrote temporary files to disk. `<executionPart>Spills` indicates the number of times the corresponding query execution stage wrote temporary files to disk.; `<executionPart>SpilledBytes` indicates the size, in bytes, of the memory released by writing temporary files to disk.; `<executionPart>SpilledDataStorageSize` indicates the size, in bytes, of disk space used for temporary files.; `<executionPart>SpilledRecords` indicates the number of records written to temporary files on disk. For more information on writing temporary files to disk, see [`allowDiskUse()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) | | 8.3 | Slow query log entries have an optional `originalQueryShapeHash` field that contains that query shape of the following operations that originate on the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#std-program-mongos) : [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find); [`aggregate`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.aggregate); [`count`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/count.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.count); [`distinct`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.distinct) The original query shape of the `mongos` operation may differ after the `mongos` sends the operation to the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-program-mongod) . MongoDB 8.3 also introduces slow in-progress query log entries. Queries trigger a slow-in progress log during execution. These logs contain less information than standard slow query logs. MongoDB logs queries at most once if the query's duration surpasses the [`operationProfiling.slowOpInProgressThresholdMs`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpInProgressThresholdMs) When an operation specifies a [time limit for a query](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents/specify-query-timeout.md#std-label-manual-query-timeout), slow query logs contain a `deadline` field. `deadline` indicates the time the operation must complete by, which is equal to the time at the start of the operation plus the value of the query timeout. | | 9.0 | When a query shape has query knobs set through [`setQuerySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) or [`setParameter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setparameter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setParameter), slow query log entries include a `queryKnobs` document. The document shows the effective value of each knob and where the value comes from, with the same shape as the [explain output](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-output-query-knobs). For details, see [Query Knobs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#std-label-setQuerySettings-query-knobs) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#version-specific-changes · keywords: Query Insights, index, query optimization, queryFramework, queryFramework: "classic", queryFramework: "sbe"

- [fact] Other $text restrictions: a query with $text cannot use hint(); text indexes do not improve sort performance; a multi-word phrase mixed with single terms matches only documents containing the full phrase; text indexes accept only binary comparison, so a collection with a non-simple collation needs collation {locale: 'simple'} on the text index; compound text indexes need equality conditions on key prefixes. — https://mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/text-index-restrictions/ · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, Atlas Search vs $text vs $regex (search offload decision)

- [passage] Some high-latency [`$lookup`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lookup.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-lookup) operations may not generate a slow query log for the foreign collection. This can occur because slow query logs correspond with operations that are reported in the [database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler), whereas latency metrics increment only when a [collection lock](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/concurrency.md#std-label-faq-concurrency-locking) is acquired. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collStats.md#high-latency-lookup-operations · keywords: Query Insights, query optimization, $lookup · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/namespace-insights.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md
- [passage] If the `$lookup` query on a shard can perform a local read, the `$lookup` doesn't record a separate operation for querying the foreign collection. A local read refers to when the query on the foreign collection targets only the same shard where the current operation is being executed. As a result, the `$lookup` operation increases the `$collStats` latency metrics and operation counts, but does not generate a slow query log for the foreign collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collStats.md#high-latency-lookup-operations · keywords: Query Insights, query optimization, $lookup, $collStats · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/namespace-insights.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/

- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `profile` | int | Configures the profiler level. The following profiler levels are available: `0`The profiler is off and does not collect any data. This is the default profiler level.`1`The profiler collects data for operations that exceed the `slowms` threshold or match a specified [filter.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setprofilinglevel.md#std-label-set-profiling-level-options-filter)When a filter is set:The `slowms` and `sampleRate` options are not used for profiling.; The profiler only captures operations that match the [filter.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setprofilinglevel.md#std-label-set-profiling-level-options-filter)`2`The profiler collects data for all operations.When set to level `2`, the profiler ignores user provided values for `slowms` and `filter`. Since profiling is not available on [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), the [`profile`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/profile.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.profile) command cannot be used to set the profiling level to a value other than `0` on a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instance. | | `slowms` | int | Optional. Default: 100 The slow operation time threshold, in milliseconds. Operations that run for longer than this threshold are considered *slow*. Slow operations are logged based on `workingMillis`, which is the amount of time that MongoDB spends working on that operation. This means that factors such as waiting for locks and flow control do not affect whether an operation exceeds the slow operation threshold. When [`logLevel`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.logLevel) is set to `0`, MongoDB records *slow* operations to the diagnostic log at a rate determined by [`slowOpSampleRate`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpSampleRate) At higher `logLevel` settings, all operations appear in the diagnostic log regardless of their latency with the following exception: the logging of slow oplog entry messages by the secondaries. The secondaries log only the slow oplog entries; increasing the `logLevel` does not log all oplog entries. This argument affects the same setting as the configuration option [`operationProfiling.slowOpThresholdMs`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpThresholdMs) | | `sampleRate` | double | Optional. Default: 1.0 The fraction of *slow* operations that should be profiled or logged. `sampleRate` accepts values between 0 and 1, inclusive. This argument affects the same setting as the configuration option [`operationProfiling.slowOpSampleRate`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpSampleRate) and does not affect the slow oplog entry log messages on secondaries. | | `filter` | object | Optional. A query that determines which operations are profiled or logged. The filter query takes the following form: `{ <field1>: <expression1>, ... }` The query can be any legal [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) operation where the query `<field>` matches a field in the [profiler output.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) This argument affects the same setting as the configuration option [`operationProfiling.filter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.filter). When `filter` is set, the `slowms` and `sampleRate` options are not used for profiling and slow-query log lines. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/profile.md#command-fields · keywords: Query Insights, query optimization, profile, The profiler collects data for operations that exceed the , slowms, sampleRate · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setProfilingLevel.md
- [passage] In rare circumstances, a write can fail due to cache pressure. - [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `createIndexes` | string | The collection for which to create indexes. | | `indexes` | array | Specifies the indexes to create. Each document in the array specifies a separate index. | | `writeConcern` | document | Optional. A document expressing the [write concern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern.md). Omit to use the default write concern. | | `commitQuorum` | integer or string | Optional. The minimum number of data-bearing replica set members (i.e. commit quorum), including the primary, that must report a successful [index build](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations-replicated-build) before the primary marks the `indexes` as ready. You can resume some [interrupted index builds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations-build-failure) when the commit quorum is set to the default `"votingMembers"`. See [`setIndexCommitQuorum`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setIndexCommitQuorum) Replica set nodes in a commit quorum must have [`members[n].buildIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-configuration.md#mongodb-rsconf-rsconf.members-n-.buildIndexes) set to `true`. If any voting nodes have `members[n].buildIndexes` set to `false`, you can't use the default `"votingMembers"` commit quorum. Either configure all nodes with `members[n].buildIndexes` set to `true`, or select a different commit quorum. Supports the following values: `"votingMembers"` - all data-bearing voting replica set members (*Default*). A "voting" member is any replica set member where [`members[n].votes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-configuration.md#mongodb-rsconf-rsconf.members-n-.votes) is greater than `0`.; `"majority"` - a simple majority of data-bearing replica set members.; `<int>` - a specific number of data-bearing replica set members.; A replica set [tag name.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/configure-replica-set-tag-sets.md) | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#command-fields · keywords: Query Insights, index, createIndexes, indexes, writeConcern, commitQuorum

- [passage] MongoDB Compass displays the COLLSCAN query stage to indicate that a collection scan was used for this query. Collection scans indicate that the mongod had to scan the entire collection document by document to identify the results. This is a generally expensive operation and can result in slow queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/ · keywords: Query Insights, index
- [passage] [ { "x.a": { $gt: 85 } }, { "x.b": { $gt: 80 } } ]` However, you can specify compound conditions on the same identifier in a single filter document, such as in the following examples: `// Example 1 [ { $or: [{"x.a": {$gt: 85}}, {"x.b": {$gt: 80}}] } ] // Example 2 [ { $and: [{"x.a": {$gt: 85}}, {"x.b": {$gt: 80}}] } ] // Example 3 [ { "x.a": { $gt: 85 }, "x.b": { $gt: 80 } } ]` For examples, see [Array Update Operations with `arrayFilters`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findandmodify.md#std-label-findAndModify-command-arrayFilters) `arrayFilters` is not available for updates that use an aggregation pipeline. | | `hint` | document or string | Optional. Specifies a document with a list of variables. This allows you to improve command readability by separating the variables from the query text. The document syntax is: `{ <variable_name_1>: <expression_1>, ..., <variable_name_n>: <expression_n> }` The variable is set to the value returned by the expression, and cannot be changed afterwards. To access the value of a variable in the command, use the double dollar sign prefix (`$$`) together with your variable name in the form `$$<variable_name>`. For example: `$$targetTotal`. To use a variable to filter results, you must access the variable within the [`$expr`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#mongodb-query-op.-expr) operator. For a complete example using `let` and variables, see [Use Variables in `let`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findandmodify.md#std-label-findAndModify-let-example) **New in version 5.0** | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findAndModify.md#command-fields · keywords: Query Insights, index,  For examples, see [Array Update Operations with , arrayFilters, hint, query

- [passage] Learn more about slow queries and get suggestions to improve database performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-performanceAdvisor.md · keywords: Query Insights, query optimization
- [passage] | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `version` | A number that indicates the query engine used to complete the query. `1` indicates that the classic engine was used.; `2` indicates that the [slot-based query execution engine](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/sbe.md#std-label-sbe-landing) was used. | | `createdFromQuery` | A document that contains the specific query that resulted in this cache entry. For example: `{ "query" : <document>, "sort" : <document>, "projection" : <document> }` | | `isActive` | A boolean that indicates whether the entry is active or inactive. If active, the query planner is currently using the entry to generate query plans.; If inactive, the query planner is not currently using the entry to generate query plans. See [Plan Cache Entry State.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-state) | | `planCacheShapeHash` | A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of the [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape). See [`explain.queryPlanner.planCacheShapeHash`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.planCacheShapeHash) Starting in MongoDB 8.0, the existing `queryHash` field is duplicated in a new field named `planCacheShapeHash`. If you're using an earlier MongoDB version, you'll only see the `queryHash` field. Future MongoDB versions will remove the deprecated `queryHash` field, and you'll need to use the `planCacheShapeHash` field instead. | | `planCacheKey` | A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of the key used to find the plan cache entry associated with this query. The plan cache key is a function of both the [plan cache query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape) and the currently available indexes for that shape. See [`explain.queryPlanner.planCacheKey`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.planCacheKey) | | `cachedPlan` | The details of the cached plan. The fields included in the `cachedPlan` vary based on whether the query was completed using the classic engine or the slot-based query execution engine. If any voting nodes have `members[n].buildIndexes` set to `false`, you can't use the default `"votingMembers"` commit quorum. Either configure all nodes with `members[n].buildIndexes` set to `true`, or select a different commit quorum. Supports the following values: `"votingMembers"` - all data-bearing voting replica set members (*Default*). A "voting" member is any replica set member where [`members[n].votes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-configuration.md#mongodb-rsconf-rsconf.members-n-.votes) is greater than `0`.; `"majority"` - a simple majority of data-bearing replica set members.; `<int>` - a specific number of data-bearing replica set members. - [fact] COMPASS-7062 (open, unassigned, Minor, reported against Compass 1.39.0 and MongoDB 6.0.7): for an aggregation with $match plus $lookup running on the classic (non-SBE) engine, the Compass explain summary counts only the documents and keys examined by the $match. It hides $lookup work such as collection scans, so a slow pipeline can look efficient. With SBE the summary is accurate. - [passage] - [atlas api performanceAdvisor enableManagedSlowMs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-performanceadvisor-enablemanagedslowms.md#std-label-atlas-api-performanceAdvisor-enableManagedSlowMs) - Enables MongoDB Cloud to use its slow operation threshold for the specified project. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-performanceAdvisor.md#related-commands · keywords: mongodb-query-optimization-tooling
- [passage] | Status | Description | | --- | --- | | `BUILDING` | The following scenarios can cause an index to be in the `BUILDING` state: MongoDB is building the index or re-building the index after an edit.; MongoDB Search cannot keep up with indexing changes to the collection. In this case, Atlas rebuilds the index in the background. When the index is in the `BUILDING` state: For a new index, MongoDB Search cannot use the index for queries until the index build is complete.; For an existing index, MongoDB Search uses the old index definition for queries until the index rebuild is complete. An index in the `BUILDING` state may be queryable or non-queryable. | | `DOES_NOT_EXIST` | The index does not exist. An index in the `DOES_NOT_EXIST` state is always non-queryable. | | `DELETING` | MongoDB is deleting the index. An index in the `DELETING` state is always non-queryable. | | `FAILED` | The index build failed. Indexes can enter the `FAILED` state due to an invalid index definition. An index in the `FAILED` state may be queryable or non-queryable. | | `PENDING` | MongoDB has not yet started building the index. An index in the `PENDING` state is always non-queryable. | | `READY` | The index is ready and can support queries. An index in the `READY` state is always queryable. | | `STALE` | The index is queryable but has stopped replicating data from the indexed collection. Searches on the index may return out-of-date data. Indexes can enter the `STALE` state due to replication errors. An index in the `STALE` state is always queryable. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/listSearchIndexes.md#mongodb-search-index-statuses · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, BUILDING, DOES_NOT_EXIST, DELETING, FAILED
